correctness.rationale: Bijection of positional embeddings with nonnegative integer weak compositions gives exact binomial count; a cut-position double count proves generalized-Eulerian coefficient formula; bounded increasing-block construction proves all possible weak descent degrees; binomial monotonicity completes histogram, with all boundaries. Literal DP and arithmetic coefficient checks independently confirmed 9,287 targets and 52,318 formal coefficient comparisons.

originality.rationale: Comparison with the same cyclic hosts in Flaxman et al. (2004) shows that its published distinct-subsequence enumerator gives support but not the full index-embedding multiplicity histogram. Kosche et al. (2021) studies absent and shortest subsequences, not positive embedding weights. General binomial word frameworks and known Eulerian distributions are explicitly acknowledged; published-record searches did not reveal the all-parameter spectrum. Residual risk of an unlocated classical specialization remains.
residual_risks: No independent external review, and a classical P-partition or word-binomial identity may encode an equivalent specialization.
The general binomial-word literature was not exhaustively inspected at full-text level; current originality conclusion reflects accessible material and explicit comparison, not a proof of uniqueness.
Finite tests do not establish the unrestricted theorem; the proof is a separate argument.

value.rationale: The uniform-deletion probability spectrum of a cyclic-periodic host is a well-defined natural all-length invariant. The theorem determines each attainable positive probability and how many outputs attain it for every alphabet size, number of periods and subsequence length, strictly strengthening known support-only counts and providing exact benchmark instances.
